For the (spin–zero) partial–wave expansion the elastic scattering amplitude is  

 f(θ)= (1/k) Σ_{l=0}^{∞} (2l+1) e^{iδ_l} sin δ_l P_l (cos θ)

Along the incident-beam (forward) direction θ = 0, so P_l(1)=1 and  

 f(0)= (1/k) Σ_{l=0}^{∞} (2l+1) e^{iδ_l} sin δ_l  
   = (1/k) Σ_{l=0}^{∞} (2l+1)[cos δ_l sin δ_l + i sin² δ_l].

Hence the imaginary part is  

 Im f(0)= (1/k) Σ_{l=0}^{∞} (2l+1) sin² δ_l.

Only the first five phase shifts are appreciable; thus  

S = Σ_{l=0}^{4} (2l+1) sin² δ_l

δ₀ = 90° → sin²δ₀ = 1     (2·0+1)=1 ⇒ 1×1 = 1  
δ₁ = 67° → sin²δ₁ = (sin 67°)² = 0.847 ⇒ 3×0.847 = 2.541  
δ₂ = 55° → sin²δ₂ = 0.671   ⇒ 5×0.671 = 3.355  
δ₃ = 30° → sin²δ₃ = 0.250   ⇒ 7×0.250 = 1.750  
δ₄ = 13° → sin²δ₄ = 0.0506  ⇒ 9×0.0506 = 0.455  

S = 1 + 2.541 + 3.355 + 1.750 + 0.455 ≈ 9.102.

For 50 MeV electrons the (non-relativistic) momentum is  

 p = √(2m_e E)  
   = √(2·0.511 MeV·50 MeV) ≈ 7.14 MeV/c.

The corresponding wave number is  

 k = p / ħc = 7.14 MeV / 197.33 MeV fm ≈ 0.0362 fm⁻¹,

so  

 1/k ≈ 27.63 fm.

Therefore  

 Im f(0) = (1/k) S ≈ 27.63 fm × 9.102 ≈ 2.51×10² fm.

Thus  

Im f(0) ≈ 251 fm, which matches option (A).

Answer: A
